description:
FILED s473t2 (Opus triage of the 152 causeless blessed sweep rows), on main 0d783d24.
Probes scratch/s473t2/probes/p11-misc.pl A and p12-evalscope.pl.

ROW BEHIND IT: perl-tests/eval.t 40 ("lexical search terminates correctly at
subroutine boundary") = 1 row.  It reads got='!' where perl reads 'good!'.

THE SHAPE (perl-tests/eval.t 184-190):
    $main::r = "good";
    sub terminal { eval '$r . q{!}' }
    is(do { my $r = "bad"; eval 'terminal($r)' }, 'good!', ...);
Perl: `$r` inside `terminal`'s eval is not in any lexical scope that reaches the
sub, so it is $main::r = "good".  PCL: the file declares `my $r` at eval.t:313,
AFTER the sub -- and the eval resolves to that (empty) cell, so the answer is '!'.

IN ISOLATION THE SAME THREE LINES AGREE (p11-misc.pl A prints good! on both), so
it is the LATER file-level `my $r` that does it.  The two-line reproducer of the
capture itself REFUSES rather than mis-resolving:
    $main::r = "good"; sub terminal { eval '$r . q{!}' }
    my $got = do { my $r = "bad"; eval 'terminal($r)' }; print $got;
    my $r = "later";
  perl: good!
  PCL : Transpile failed: Parser2 TODO: file lexical 'r' captured by sub terminal
so the file-lexical capture machinery has a path where it refuses and a path
where it silently captures a declaration that is not in scope at the use.  The
scope question is "is the declaration BEFORE this use in the file", the same
question #454 answered for signature parameters.
subject: BUG (string-eval capture, #296 family): an unqualified `$name` inside a string eval in a NAMED sub binds a FILE lexical declared LATER in the file instead of the package variable -- perl-tests/eval.t 40
